Added: Provide opt-in ICU-backed Unicode exact-name and prefix queries with canonical-equivalent matching and explicit accent-insensitive modes.
Offer grapheme-aware fuzzy location suggestions with bounded edit distances, adjacent-transposition support and deterministic ranked scores.
Expose lazy per-level streaming and independently measured cold and warm query latency distributions.
Changed: Defer construction of administrative ID and name indexes until the requested lookup requires them, preserving existing source models and identifiers.
Replace redundant hierarchy flattening allocations with direct traversal and bounded scoped search caches.
Keep Unicode dictionaries lazy with a two-index retention limit and prune impossible fuzzy candidates before edit-distance evaluation.
Fixed: Preserve every same-name administrative identity and parent association without silently overwriting source records.
Reject orphaned hierarchy records, duplicate numeric source identities and invalid packaged dataset records before accepting a hierarchy.
Preserve order and object identity in nested model collections and parent-scoped prefix results.
Remove an undeclared ctype extension dependency from core dataset loading and geographic export validation.
Keep patch release notes isolated from the v2.0.0 major-version upgrade warning.
Security: Reject malformed UTF-8, empty Unicode search queries and oversized search inputs before expensive normalization or indexing.
Preserve distinct source IDs for Unicode-equivalent names and avoid treating visually confusable text as authoritative identity.
Keep optional Intl functionality isolated so legacy PHP search works without the extension.
Documentation: Document stable query semantics, optional Unicode runtime requirements and bounded fuzzy-search complexity.
Publish inspectable memory profiles, seeded property-based test evidence and before-and-after lookup benchmarks.
Explain legacy dataset provenance, GIS publication limits and the independent checks required before tagging a stable release.
Upgrade: Existing v2.0.0 application method signatures remain unchanged; the new Unicode APIs are opt-in and require ext-intl when used.
No Laravel service provider, mandatory database or third-party runtime service is introduced by this patch.
